source.title: GHCR image builds fail with uppercase repository owners

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

GitHub Actions image workflows can fail when the repository owner contains uppercase letters. The workflow can create an image reference such as `ghcr.io/Youness331/n8n-benchmark:latest`. Docker rejects this reference because image names must be lowercase.

### To Reproduce

1. Run an affected image build workflow in a repository or fork with an uppercase owner name.
2. Check the image reference created by the workflow.
3. See the build fail with `repository name must be lowercase`.

### Expected behavior

The workflow should use a lowercase owner in every GHCR image reference so the image build can continue.

### Debug Info

This is a GitHub Actions workflow issue, not an n8n runtime issue. The observed error was: `invalid tag ghcr.io/Youness331/n8n-benchmark:latest: repository name must be lowercase`.

## Environment

- Operating System: GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runner
- n8n Version: Not applicable; this issue affects CI workflows
- Node.js Version: Not applicable; the image reference fails validation
- Database: Not applicable; no n8n instance is running
- Execution mode: Not applicable; no n8n instance is running
- Hosting: GitHub Actions; not an n8n-hosted instance

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: The current workflow source uses `${{ github.repository_owner }}` directly in the benchmark image tag (`.github/workflows/build-benchmark-image.yml:41`). The same unnormalized value also appears in the base-image workflow (line 140), node-pc workflow (lines 74–96), and release-channel workflow (lines 154–164). A shared lowercased owner value, reused for GHCR image references, would address the benchmark case and these other paths too. This is a source review; I have not run the affected workflows.
